findings.reason: the plan must name `discovery_file_scope` (and `serve.discover_plans`) as the nesting entry and say the existing scope is made to join the region, or the node implements a mechanism that cannot satisfy its own done-when on the real call path.
findings.text: the Deliverable says `reckon/metadata_index.py` "gains a context manager … [where] a nested entry reuses the region already open", entered at `mcp._roadmap`'s top, but the module already holds that context manager — `discovery_file_scope()` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:98-106`) — and it *replaces* the region (`_DISCOVERY_FILES.set({})`) rather than joining it; it is entered by `serve.discover_plans` (`reckon/serve.py:1418,1422`), which runs inside every roadmap call, and the measurement above shows two of the six per-call `_covered_files` passes (reckon/docs 4815 directory checks, nova/docs 1239) happening inside exactly that scope; a worker who adds a joining region at `mcp._roadmap`'s top and leaves `discovery_file_scope` as it stands gets one pass per call shared among the four `scope_open=False` readers only, so each covered directory is still checked twice and the done-when bullet "at most once per call" is unreachable — while a single-project synthetic tree used by the gate need not exercise the nested scope at all and can pass

findings.reason: §46's residual (~9 s) is the input "a following section takes … as its input", and a reduction larger than the stat time available understates the residual that section is dispatched against.
findings.text: "Taken with §45, this removes at most about 12.5 s … about 4.1 s from §45, plus the 4.65 s of directory checks and the 3.8 s discovery walk here" adds two figures that overlap: `serve._walk_discovery_signature` (`reckon/serve.py:1239-1252`) reaches `_dir_identity` itself, through `metadata_index._covered_files_for_project` → `_covered_files` → `_reuse_covered` (`reckon/metadata_index.py:683→647→347→758`), so its 3.8 s is cumulative over the same stat calls that make up `_dir_identity`'s 4.65 s; the same Why also states the whole 21.7 s call "spends 7.0 s in 29,958 `posix.stat` calls", and 4.65 + 3.8 = 8.45 s exceeds that budget
